item.title: Knock Box (Seeking Greenlighting)
item.description: a black box that when a user hears said knocking they are tempted to open it
item.content:encoded:
The premise is pretty simple as it is a black box that when a user hears said knocking they are tempted to open it but they end up dead.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlighting: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mysterious

Page Layout: Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: Imagine if you take a walk in the forest silent and you see a random black box just sitting there you feel no attraction to it until you hear it knock twice, your suddenly now just have to look at that box you don't know why you have to always look at it but it just feels like you should. Again the box knocks and this time you go to the box standing right next to you glee with excitement and you open the box a holy light shines through like a video game chest and… you dropped to the ground, the box closes and you die of a heart attack.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The black Box is a simple looking box or crate with a unknown brand stuck on the top it is a sticker on the left side of the box are other stickers saying "Every thing you would LOVE!" with pictures of a smiling family on it. The right side of the box reads "Are you having a rough time? containing in this very box you'll find the best things that will cheer you up!" although on the bottom of the box it reads in a black sticker "Silly you! this is the Bottom of the product!". After random increments of time the box begins knocking at the first 5 knocks the subject just simply examines the box, but after the 6th knock subject forcefully decide to open the box any attempts to stop said subject has always failed. subject that are going to open the box seem to not be affected by any sort of damage until said heart attack occurs. Subjects do indeed take physical damage but some how do not die until said heart attack. when subjects open the box or are about to there heart rate begins to rise and facial expressions begin to always show extreme excitement before open the box which there is a small chance that the pull out something out the box which at that point should be contained in a simple non see through bag. as soon as subject dies said box will close no matter what attempts of keep the box opened had failed. upon opening the box will show a bright yellowish light will glitter inside the box, the amount of objects in the box is unknown. objects inside the box seem to be quite simple man made objects of again unknown brand these objects include: pencils, blankets, coffee cups with coffee inside, toy cars, walkie-talkies, glass jars, gold bars, etc. each test of every subject pulls out a different object. it is presumed that the objects are what the subject wants or craves for.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The box is sure from its look it looks like a ordinary box but no matter the cause if someone hears that knock more than 6 times they always will get through what ever is in the way, (audio recording of the knock do not activate the reaction) the same effect happens with animals as well.

Additional Notes: None as of 12/1/2020

item.title: "The Gardener" [Seeking Greenlight]
item.description: A humanoid that must create less-than-obedient "drones" from plants and the unfortunate actions that follow.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Split across multiple iterations of the document spanning across 10 years as containment procedures and behavior of the SCP object change.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid who, by being near plant matter, accelerates their growth dramatically, and rather than bringing them into old age, makes matured plants into sentient "drones", dubbed SCP-XXXX-1, later -2 and -3, as the nature of the anomaly changes. While it begins as a child who turns plants into not terribly threatening sentient and hostile plants, later creations of SCP-XXXX display anomalous growths and sapience, making them more threatening. SCP-XXXX is not able to stop these events from happening, as it must be near living plants in order to live, and has no control of these creatures, often being prone to attack from them.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is given its anomalous properties through the containment breach of a reality bender in a site near SCP-XXXX's home. A month after this breach, the Foundation investigates reports of deaths in a forest inhabited by SCP-XXXX, who had inadvertently converted several plants into SCP-XXXX-1 instances. An MTF unit is sent to find the source of these deaths, containing SCP-XXXX. Containment procedures begin simple, with only a modified humanoid containment chamber with a grass floor, as grass is found to be a non-issue when converted to SCP-XXXX-1. While SCP-XXXX grows over the span of a decade, containment procedures become more complex as it begins to generate SCP-XXXX-2 and -3 instances, eventually resulting either in the object's termination or a command to terminate it should it attempt to breach containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main draw of the concept is SCP-XXXX-1+, and how their severity impacts the life and conditions of SCP-XXXX, who isn't really a catalyst for any events as much as its creations.

Additional Notes: My biggest concern is that sapient, hostile plant-monsters feels like a concept that's simply not threatening enough to warrant the drastic actions that I want the narrative to take. I've been toying around with different ideas on this matter, foremost being to make SCP-XXXX marginally stronger than a small group of people with sufficient plants nearby, and/or to slowly give SCP-XXXX plant-like qualities, causing its anomaly to take effect on itself, posing a security threat, but these are distateful to me both for fear of X-man syndrome, as well as the fact that the narrative simply isn't really that much about the humanoid. Any advice on this situation specifically would be greatly appreciated.

item.title: The Island of Lies (Seeking Greenlights)
item.description: An Island that scrambles one's memories and leaves them much different than they were before.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

+ Elevator Pitch
- Hide
  • An island that will attempt to put any visitors to sleep. They will wake up on an identical island a ways away with some of their memories changed out. This can be anything from simple things like where they put their keys to aspects of their identity and personality itself.
  • People can go through this process an infinite number of times, further altering their memories and personality each time.
+ Central Narrative
- Hide

My goal with this is to focus on two subjects the Foundation has been using to test the SCP.

The first subject is a person who has been hit incredibly hard by the memory alterations, to the point where very few of his original memories still exist. This subject is being rehabilitated by Foundation staff in an attempt to see if he can be restored to his former self or if the changes are permanent.

The other subject is being used to test the effects of repeatedly sending the same person to the island. This subject also has barely any of his original memories remaining and has changed names at least three times, but rather than attempting to "fix" him, the researchers are simply layering on more and more changes to his brain. This part of the article would probably be more comedic in tone than the rest.

+ Hook/Attention Grabber and Additional Notes
- Hide

The big things I want people to be drawn to are the mystery of why and how the memory changes are being made as well as the stories of the two test subjects.

Additional Notes:
I want to know if the second island is really necessary, considering how small of a role it plays in the big picture. I was also playing around with the idea of the SCP being sentient and afraid of rising sea levels, let me know what you think of that idea.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight ("The Boo Hag")
item.description: Looks can be deceiving, but not in the way you may think.
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I’m a long-time lurker and looking for critique on the concept for my first SCP. All feedback is welcome.

Seeking Greenlights: YES

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Traditional SCP document layout.

Elevator Pitch: What is perceived as a horrid monster in Gullah culture/Carolinian folklore is, in reality, a caring mother. While not necessarily benevolent, this SCP does whatever it takes to care for its child.

Central Narrative:

+ Open
- Close

The narrative is intended to be told throughout the entire document, from the containment procedures, to the description, to a small collection of recovered documents and interviews. The SCP itself is what can be described as a “boo hag:” a skinless, humanoid entity that has the ability to disguise itself using victims’ skins, bewitch others using its voice, and transfer the life force it drains from victims to strengthen and heal other boo hags. Through the RD’s and interviews, the reader learns that the SCP and its daughter were hunted by humans; the latter was killed while the former escaped at the cost of losing her tongue. Having lost its daughter and ability to bewitch, the hag bides its time and waits for another chance to raise a child. Sometime later, the hag infiltrates a family under the guise of the patriarch’s late wife’s sister and cares for the patriarch's daughter, who is suffering from a terminal illness. The hag uses its powers to drain and transfer the life forces of local victims into her new daughter, but fails to keep her alive. The daughter expires, and the hag is apprehended by authorities following missing persons accounts. The Foundation intervenes and contains the hag; investigation of the daughter’s body reveals her to have been a young boo hag. The reader is left to decide whether or not the man’s late wife was also Boo Hag and to question the origins of the “Daughter Hag.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Open
- Close
  • Explores a twist on the “murder monster” cliche and on a lesser known creature associated with Gullah culture and Carolinian folklore
  • The SCP builds up to a final reveal that will (hopefully) explain why the SCP is passive in containment (has no desire to lose another child), give a reason for the SCP to use its powers in the first place, why it infiltrated that certain family, and offer the right amount of ambiguity so as not to water down the intrigue of the SCP down with a concrete answer.

Additional Notes: I realize that choosing to write a humanoid SCP as my first article may be looked down upon, but I believe that I have what it takes to tell a compelling story.

item.title: The Dover Demon
item.description: The creature known as "The Dover Demon" witnesses the history of the world.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy/History

Elevator Pitch: SCP-X is the creature known as The Dover Demon. SCP-X is a sapient small humanoid with bright white eyes lacking pupils, with a large skull and and no mouth, however it is able to speak, with its face moving as if it is speaking. It also has 4 long fingers. SCP-X is also able to become invisible, to hide itself from others. SCP-X is very friendly (and rather humorous) and likes interacting with trusted individuals. It typically walks on all four of its legs, but is capable of walking on its two hind legs. SCP-X has a high interest in floors, and anything on them, such as rugs, crumbs, shoes, and the shoes people are wearing.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

The main focus of the article will be centered around an interview conducted with SCP-X shortly after its recovery. SCP-X is asked about where its from. This leads to a brief explanation that he was born in a cave, and that once he was around 19 he left his family and his cave, and started to explore the world. He then begins talking about how as he traveled, there was a lot of sounds: birds and mammals probably, but he was focused on the grassy fields and the smell of fresh soil.

He then goes on about how the fields eventually stopped, and he came to a place with big buildings and a bunch of people. And he goes on about how amazing these peoples shoes were, all black and shiny with neatly tied laces, and the ground was all neat and organized, with nice tiles. He then goes on about how he wandered around a bit, the buildings eventually got smaller, and eventually the ground stopped, and he was peering into a body of water. He wanted to keep going and see more shiny shoes, so he spotted a big ship nearby labeled "The Mayflower" and hopped on.

He says that the ground wasn't sturdy on the mayflower, and peoples shoes weren't shiny and laced, either. People wore old brown shoes with loose laces, and they often fell off of their feet. It was like this for a while, until eventually the boat stopped, and everyone started cheering. They all started getting off the boat on to a rock, and started setting up camps on the grassy fields.

The described that now that he was back on land, he could continue his journey on the neat paths. The problem was that there weren't any paths, just a lot of people in yucky shoes and grass. So he decided to stick around for a while.

Eventually, the people started organizing the ground, with rocks and stones. It wasn't as neat and clean as they were before, but it'd have to do. They still had dirty shoes though, which he didn't like. But eventually, people in red coats carrying long guns started appearing, and they had spectacular black shiny shoes. He started following them around, and learned a bit about them. They liked to push people in dirty shoes, "probably telling them to get new ones".

he explains that one time, there was a big group of people yelling at a bunch of the people with red coats and shiny shoes. Eventually, the red coated people started shooting at the people in the crowd, who started spilling blood all over the tidy ground. He didn't like the ground to be messy, so he left. But soon enough there was a lot of shooting and a lot of blood, which went on for a long time, until it all stopped and people finally started getting new shoes. The people in the red coats had left, probably because they didn't need to push people because of their shoes anymore.

SCP-X goes on to describe a few more brief details in his life, like how eventually big boxes with wheels started driving around on roads, and how shoes got more colorful, and eventually, he was caught by the SCP Foundation. The interview ends with SCP-X looking under the table, and asks the interviewer if he can try on his fancy shoes.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think the attention grabber that the foundation literally has a little guy who was aboard the mayflower and was present at the Boston Massacre, but is just talking about everyone's shoes.

Additional Notes: I've always had some interest in the Dover Demon, and thought of this idea that might fit him. Give me your critiques and tell me what you think!

item.title: The Song of Your Life (Seeking Greenlights)
item.description: anomalous radio that plays music for who ever enters
item.content:encoded:
An anomalous radio that plays music for who ever enters its radius. Such music can only be described as 'fitting' for the person in-question.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Musical

Page Layout (Optional): Basic layout

Elevator Pitch:
-SCP is a sentient vintage ham radio that produces various forms of music to living things that enter its radius.
-The music in-question is based off the person's history, personality, how other people view them and in the case of other SCPs or other anomalous entities, their abilities. It can also play music to what would otherwise fit the scenario in-question (if its a containment breach its going to sound out chase music mixed in with the leitmotifs of the other SCPs that are part of the breach, etc, etc.)
-The SCP can teleport to a place that is having a suitably dramatic moment and play said music or otherwise to a person that it has played music to before and is 'bored.'

+ show block
– hide block

]
Central Narrative: As above with potentially exploring other SCP's stories and personalities through the radio's music. Eventually (I don't really know how planned interviews and addendum later down the SCP's life-line works) I'm planning for a researcher to try and ask the SCP questions, the SCP answers in a semi-convoluted way.

Standard questions apply and then… the researcher will go to ask 'do you have a song of yourself?'

The radio will reply 'no' but will than go onto say, 'but I'm sure I did have one, but I don't anymore.'

And like… that could go down so many routes, who took it? Where is it now? How do we get it? What happens when the SCP gets its 'song' back?

Does the Foundation fulfill its request? The SCP probably has some hints in its memory of where the song once was and that can go into tales or more interviews and mission ops and lot of other things.

So that's a narrative I've come up with.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I've looked over other SCPs for a while now and while there are a couple that do involve music, there are none that I could find that involve the SCP finding the theme song of basically anything in existence… except itself. Of a most important note including other SCPs that could delve into one's personality or backstory through usage of music.

Additional Notes: No particular concerns right now.

item.title: The Watch | Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Other, General Information about SCPs with abilities.

Elevator Pitch:

  • A Watch the can open portal in space and time allowing the user to travel through time and even

different dimensions (dimensions only if the user has seen the dimension.

  • A Old Black and White Tv that houses the sales commercial for the watch in a form of a 80's style

advertisement.

  • A Male salesman in the commercial that will hand you the watch if the viewer wishes to purchase

the watch for $15.99.

  • Tv will go dormant for a few months after a purchase is made.

Central Narrative: A Watch that can create portals through space and time sold to a viewer through a black and white tv by a 1.3m tall white male with bold hair and blue eyes. After the "salesman" finishes talking about the product he will ask the viewer if they would like to purchase the watch. If the viewer agrees then the salesman will reach id hand through the tv maintaining the black and white texture and ask for a payment of $15.99. Once payed the salesman will place the money into his pocket and hand a box to the viewer then the TV will turn off and remain dormant for 2-3 months.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As far as I know there isn't really anything like this but the concept I think is pretty interesting because of how the object is obtained and what it can do. This is why i will require clearance level 4 in order to interact with the watch, tv or salesman and the SCP will receive a safe class because it's not going anywhere without help.

Additional Notes: I'm wondering if there is anything like this already on the site, if it's a good and article worthy subject and if there is anything about the SCP that would benefit from change, keep in mind i wish to keep this a safe or thaumiel class SCP. Thankyou :)

item.title: A Balkan fairy tail
item.description: Seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout (Optional): The article is made out of several camera and audio footages.

Elevator Pitch: The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her. Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is atacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while runing from the still alive insurgent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict. In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again. The insurgent atacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local offical army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out. Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village. Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and is stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bulet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is about old conflicts that were never resolved coming to light. Bojana represents a generation not bound to those conflicts and has a future that she can choose freely, while Kosta, Sam and the people of Bosnia are chained to their fate.

item.title: Idea: Intertemporal Boots (Stay With Me Here)
item.description: allows them to walk through time so to speak
item.content:encoded:
A pair of boots that causes the user to move through space normally, but also allows them to walk through time so to speak.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

The SCP is a pair of boots. They would either be made from cloth and have a magical 'Serpent's Hand' sort of feel, or be completely robotic/futuristic. The file would go over the basic mechanics of the boots and testing would include D-Class being thrown throughout various time periods only to have the Foundation return them via some sort of temporal anchor.

Nothing crazy at first, walking forward on the x and z axis causes the user to jump forward in time. Walking backward on the x and z-axis causes them to jump backward in time. The file should get weirder when the D-Class starts moving on the y-axis. This segment would be heavily redacted/classified, but I think the file should imply that the D-Class is visiting other timelines that lay parallel to our own. (It's this part were I would need the most help on brainstorming ideas.)

Just an idea, but it would be a real hoot to write. I'm aiming for more of a Series I/II feel with this article. Nothing world-ending about this SCP, just some anomalous dimension shifting.

item.title: Emergent Ego (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: read certain SCP files in a particular order, and become possessed
item.content:encoded:
read certain SCP files in a particular order, and become possessed by some unknown personality that emerges and overwhelms your own personality.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Sci-Fi / Esoteric

Elevator Pitch: Exposure to particular combinations of SCP files, or the knowledge therein, results in the emergence of deviant archetypal personalities with anomalous properties, which override the ego of the subject viewing the files; read certain SCP files, and become possessed by some unknown personality.

Central Narrative: Discovered when a Class-B staff member experienced a psychological break accompanied by anomalous change in personality, physiology, and working esoteric knowledge; review of foundation records revealed a similar incident in the past.

+ show block
– hide block

The only known commonality between the incidents is the exposure to a particular set of case files over a period of six months. These files, known in combination as [SCP Number]-1, represent one of possibly numerous patterns that cause archetypal emergence.

In the case of [SCP Number]-1, the emergence of the accompanying personality was retroactively associated with a number of symptoms prior to complete ego eclipse. These all occur prior to the full emergence of the archetypical personality. A psychological profile of the emergent personality is nonetheless included based on the data available.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Research ongoing: one D-Class personnel is to be exposed to the pattern of SCP files to try and replicate an emergence event. In addition, Foundation researchers, aided by onsite supercomputers, are parsing incident reports for similar commonalities to indicate additional patterns and corresponding archetypes.

Additional Notes: This SCP is meant to serve a dual purpose, as a frame story for an SCP podcast that I'm working on — I want to be up front that this is ultimately my intention, but I still fully believe that the idea can stand alone as an entry, and in no way am I trying to create a subpar SCP just to enable a related venture. My primary goal is to make this SCP happen, and, should it be approved and see some success, I'll then explore additional creative avenues with it.

The podcast will be from the perspective of the D-Class personnel being exposed to articles (under the pretense of reading and recording them for accessibility use within the Foundation). The D-Class in question will slowly deteriorate into this emergent personality over the course of the podcast, as a part of the overarching narrative.

Seeking Green light: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Elevator Pitch:A photo album that can predict disasters and death.
Central Narrative: A long explanation of how the photo album works. It shows photos of a woman in various places, from various time periods. Depending on how long the viewer has to live, the woman will appear to be a different age. The places she appears in the photos are sites of famous disasters shortly before they happened, such as 9/11 or Chernobyl. The article ends with the writer speculating they could use the book to predict containment breaches or disasterous experiments by having their personnel look at the book, but then there's an addendum. A new photo has appeared in the book, and the background is the SCP site it's being held in.
Hook: Through the course of the story, the book seems relatively harmless (if a little disturbing) but some things, like the name of the site it's held at, are redacted for unclear reasons. Then at the end, why it was redacted becomes clear, and it raises whole new questions about the true nature of the book and the future.
Additional notes: This might be more a question for full draft editing, but I'm not sure whether to spice it up with more speculations or hints about how dangerous the book actually is, or whether to keep it more passive or mysterious. (Adding notes from one researcher to another, test logs, etc.)

Central Narrative: When Emperor Maximilian I went to Mexico to take the throne, whether knowingly or not, a collection of his "cousins" came with him. While they've managed to fly relatively below the radar until now, a series of disappearances and particularly gruesome recovered bodies along the US/Mexico border have sparked interest.

When a cell phone is recovered with one of the bodies, and holds a picture of what is deemed a "malformed humanoid" a detachment from the UIU is sent to take over the investigation, as it still seems plausible that this could be connected to a relatively mundane criminal or group that has something "mildly" extraordinary at their disposal.

The investigation eventually carries the group into discovering the lair employed by this specific family. They would prefer to requisition back up of course, but something, perhaps the presence of still live victims, forces their hand to move in ahead of schedule… Or, maybe they do get proper "prep time" to even the odds.

Either way, we get the climactic battle between the two groups, and maybe implications that this isn't the only such branch out there. They equate power with status, perhaps the UIU has only encountered a "minor" baron?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: An old fashioned "monster battle" adventure story with the Bureau. Can they eke out a win?

Additional Notes: Phone posted, so this is especially truncated.

item.title: It Will Not Leave
item.description: A grieved MTF officer cannot let his dead squadmate go
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Interviews and incident logs to be included.

Elevator Pitch: : An MTF officer starts to spot in random situations a former squad companion who died in an earlier Containment operation. Despite Foundation help with amnestics, the visions become more frequent and intense.

Central Narrative: Adam and Samuel have been friends since nursery times: they attended the same high school and joined the police academy at the same time. After some time in a police station, they are recruited by the SCP Foundation to join a MTF. Some years later, during a Containment operation, Samuel fails to follow protocol and ends up with Adam dead. The grief and sense of guilt pursuits Samuel to the point that starts to see Adam during his routine more often with time, to the point that jeopardizes other companions during some MTF operations. After a psychological test, he is given an amnestic to forget about his friend and stick to the MTF.

+ show block
– hide block

However, after some time without issues, during an intense MTF operation, Samuel provokes a containment breach as he claims that an unknown individual appeared to him. This appearance will never leave from then on. After providing a description to the psychologist, matching that of Adam, he is given another amnestic. The entity does not disappear though, and it starts to directly intervene in Adam’s actions, deterring him from any basic activity. Foundation demotes him and keeps him a study subject in order to prevent further failed operations, classifying Adam’s apparition as an SCP object. Eventually, Samuel commits suicide. An MTF operative from Samuel’s former MTF squad is recorded in a tapped phone call claiming that he has spotted Samuel in his garden and is afraid of reporting this to the Foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Adam’s apparition to Samuel is not real. It is driven by strong feelings of guilt, grief and melancholy. The abnormality comes from the exaggerated expression of these feelings, which get so stuck to Samuel and his subconscious that even amnestics cannot fully support Samuel. So to avoid jeopardizing future operations, Foundation classifies it as an anomaly. Samuel’s sorrow becomes a memetic effect.

Additional Notes: There are two main ideas that I wanted to explore. First, how even long-term friendship can deeply mark an individual; and second, the HRM policy of the Foundation regarding its MTF operatives, and the perils of mental health mismanagement.

Hello, readers and reviewers of the Foundation Universe!

This month's random question is: what kind of random thoughts keep you up at night?

Let's start off with some things to take a look at to enhance your reading, now that you're a site member:

  • If you have any questions about the Foundation'verse and its various individuals and groups of interest, head over to the Foundation Universe forum to talk about the various aspects of living/working/being in constant fear of a world where anomalies are real.

  • Want to leave a comment or read others' thoughts on something you've read recently? Scroll down to the bottom of that page you read, click the "Discuss" link, and take a look at the comments others have posted!

For those looking to put your knowledge of the SCP-verse to work and contribute to the site by helping develop works-in-progress, head on over to the Writing Help forums!

item.title: SCP-5233
item.content:encoded:
Big big big thanks to my lovely reviewers in chat: Pratten, Savan, Calibri_Bold, Mars, chaucer345, and Karakatt for all your wonderful suggestions to better develop the backstory here!

Image source is here: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Common_earwig_(Forficula_auricularia)_on_thumb.jpg

Notes:
- All of Wiggy’s interview excerpt dialogue consists of words found in the Wikipedia article for Earwig: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earwig
- Why earwigs? 1. When I was in elementary school, my friends and I found a very large pincher bug on the playground and admired it. Some other kid picked it up and tore off its pincers to keep as a souvenir. That image has stuck with me for over a decade. I can’t smush earwigs anymore. Also last month I found one in a box at work the other day and I let him go outside and it reminded me of that incident. 2. Quoth Wikipedia, “Earwigs are among the few non-social insect species that show maternal care.” Pinchy pinch moms are good moms. There’s a lot of neat facts about earwigs.
- Why Arizona? During my background research, I found this: https://cals.arizona.edu/yavapai/anr/hort/byg/archive/earwig.html so I just went with Arizona.

Best wishes to everyone in this crazy year. To everyone who has the opportunity to nurture a life, no matter how small, and those who teach others to do the same, you are the hope of the world.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Drama

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, and has its general appearance as a tall black figure that has devoid facial features, and no sign of hair, nose, eyes, has unchecked limitations, and numerous of anomalous abilities. In all of which, it is in foundation custody. The Foundation's goal was to prevent its anomalous abilities from attempting to cause out an event of containment breaches by accident. The containment procedure was to keep SCP-XXXX inside a 16 x 60 ft (about 3.7 x 5.5m) room constructed out of tungsten.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid entity dressed up in a bartender suit of the mid-1900s, comprised of a white shirt, a black or red tie, black trousers, and black shoes. It measures 6 to 15 feet tall has a general appearance as a tall black figure. However, it is possible that this is not SCP-XXXX's true form and that it is an eldritch being that cannot comprehend whose proper form. Its face is pitch black, utterly devoid of facial features. However, despite lacking facial features, SCP-XXXX can sense when its targets are near at all times, as it never hesitates and always sees the targets around it. SCP-XXXX has various anomalous abilities that the Foundation was to yet discovered. The ones learned so far are based on the logs of the incident, description, experiments, and interviewing logs of the Foundation, which are:

+ show block
– hide block
  • Teleportation.
  • Selective invisibility
  • Change height and body shape
  • Mind-affecting.
  • Memory adding, erasing, and inhibiting.
  • Causing instant death by making eye contact with a subject longer than three (3) seconds.
  • Extremely high superhuman attributes.
  • Causing out technological disruption upon devices at random times without wanting it to happen.
  • Able to sense how dangerous the ones it confronts are.
  • Cause out phenomenons to become omnipresent being and warp space and time between locations.
  • Strong regenerative healing factor.
  • SCP-XXXX's skin causes out common diseases that could lead to the death of those who touch it.
  • Able to sprout out tendrils that're sustainable towards all harmful things in any place of its body.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an SCP with an unknown past and various extremely dangerous and powerful anomalous abilities.

Additional Notes: This is just a short description of my SCP. The full description is still in my sandbox.

These people are now known as SCP-XXX-1(Subject) and -2(victim). When the victim is killed, the doll reverts to its original form and repairs all damage, the subject will then lose their memory of interacting with the doll. After event XXX-01, it is discovered that the doll has a cognitohazard effect that makes people want to use it.

+ show block

item.title: The Stalker (Looking for Green Light)
item.description: A SCP that is always around a present
item.content:encoded:
A SCP that is always around a present, first you just saw it once at work, now no matter where you are it is always there.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Emotional

Elevator Pitch: The idea is a SCP that slowly creeps into the victim's life. At first he’s a random face in the street, not unlike the hundreds of unknown faces you pass everyday. But over time he's just there more often, now he's at the commissary, at your favorite restaurant, and you swear you saw him through your front window. Wait was he that person you just saw out the corner of your eye? This process then repeats but quicker with hearing him everywhere and then even quicker with feeling his presence everywhere. After this it seems he's not only around you at all times, but now he's in your head. Every moment, every thought he's there.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP article will be told through a series of interviews and documents. The central story is a chronological story told by a series of interviews and other documents. It starts with a victim recounting his story as defined in the hook below, and then followed by his missing papers. This man is the first known victim of the SCP and causes the SCP foundation to launch an operation into the man's town to try and find the SCP (told through a OPORD). While they do find the SCP it escapes by unknown means but one of the SCP agents gets infected by the SCP and is put into quarantine. After a month in quarantine being a SCP scientist checking on the Agent is infected and the Agent seemingly disappeared. (see additional notes below) The infected scientist escapes to the original victim's town, the rest of the story is researching and testing why the SCP is attracted to here.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook will be an interview between a SCP Scientist and a SCP victim. In the interview the victim, clearly traumatized by what's happening to him, recounts his story of how the SCP is everywhere. It's basically the elevator pitch in more detail and in more detail.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure if this is similar to any other SCP, please tell me if it is. Note the final step after the SCP is always present in the victim's mind is eventually the victim becomes the SCP, still the same person, but now that person is the SCP.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Fireproof SAR Dog
item.description: I’m looking for a greenlight for my SCP article idea.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Containment Procedures, Description, Recovered Incident Reports, Email Transcript

Genre: Dramatic, with some lighthearted moments between the dog and it’s handler

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is simultaneously able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it and spit small sparks. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and ignorant of the animal's abilities. The dog and the handler were close with the local fire department and went on missions almost exclusively related to local fires and their aftermaths.

Central Narrative: The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through the local fire department’s incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident. The handler is entirely human and simply good at their job. The dog’s anomalous protection does not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This happens because of an off-duty incident when the dog and it’s handler are approached by a mother and her three children while relaxing at a park. The handler is distracted talking with the mother, while the children entertain themselves with the dog. Eventually, the dog becomes irritated by the attention and attacks them, biting one child and barking at the rest. This would result in the bitten child having a severe third degree burn from the bite and the other two children having small second degree burns from the dog’s saliva, sprayed from its barking. This portion of the story would be told by a hospital’s incident report that is also recovered by the Foundation.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained and it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident are amnestized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I’ve revised most of this request according to the criticism I've gotten. Hopefully this version fixes most of the inadequacies present in the request’s previous version.

Additional Notes: My plan is to make this article fairly straightforward and short given that this is my first. I’m not expecting it to be greenlit quite yet, but I would appreciate any continued criticism or suggestion. In particular, whether the concept seems viable or whether I should rewrite the concept entirely.
